why: Doc half checks out; the consequence does not. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: deep-links.md:163 reads exactly 'To prevent registration entirely, set [`disableDeepLinkRegistration`](/docs/en/settings) to `"disable"` in `settings.json`.' The rest of that two-sentence line only adds managed-settings enforcement, so it does not reverse the claim. (2) CITED LINE ACCURATE: apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:190-198 calls app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient(DEEPLINK_SCHEME) unconditionally (:193 dev branch, :197 production) with no setting consulted; `grep -ran disableDeepLinkRegistration` over the repo hits only the doc-sweep JSON/markdown artifacts, never code; MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534) carries no equivalent. (3) CONSEQUENCE FALSE ON THREE COUNTS. (a) WRONG SUBSYSTEM. Claude's key gates the CLI, which lazily writes a user-level handler (~/Applications/Claude Code URL Handler.app, a .desktop file, HKCU\Software\Classes\claude-cli) when you send your first interactive prompt (deep-links.md:153-159). Nessy has no CLI-side handler at all: setAsDefaultProtocolClient appears only in the Electron main process (one src hit, plus its build output in apps/electron/dist/main.cjs); apps/cli registers nothing. The GUI's scheme is declared STATICALLY in the bundle -- apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:82-84 `protocols: - name: Nessy Desktop / schemes: [nessy]` -- which electron-builder turns into CFBundleURLTypes in Info.plist, NSIS registry entries on Windows, and MimeType=x-scheme-handler/nessy on Linux. (b) THE IMPLIED REMEDY WOULD NOT WORK. Gating index.ts:193/197 on a setting cannot 'prevent registration entirely': LaunchServices and the installer have already registered the scheme from the installed bundle, and setAsDefaultProtocolClient only selects the DEFAULT handler among claimants. So this is not the missing off-switch for the auto-send finding -- flipping it off would leave nessy:// still routed to the app. (c) THE SCHEME IS LOAD-BEARING HERE, UNLIKE CLAUDE'S. nessy://auth-callback / nessy://auth-complete is the OAuth redirect target (packages/shared/src/auth/callback-server.ts:41; carved out at apps/electron/src/main/deep-link.ts:111-114 and packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/system.ts:83), and nessy:// doubles as the app's INTERNAL navigation transport (system.ts:283-312 routes internal nessy:// links over RPC without ever touching the OS). Claude's claude-cli:// carries only the optional launch-a-terminal convenience, so switching it off costs nothing there; a key with Claude's exact semantics would break sign-in in this fork. Also a deliberate product-shape difference: Nessy Desktop is an Electron GUI, not a terminal CLI, so the feature the setting exists to disable -- click a link, a terminal emulator opens with a pre-filled prompt -- does not exist to be disabled. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3.
correctedState: The identifier is genuinely absent (no disableDeepLinkRegistration anywhere; no equivalent in MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS), and apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:190-198 does register the scheme unconditionally -- but the finding names the wrong subsystem and the wrong layer. Claude's key gates a CLI that lazily writes a user-level handler on first prompt; Nessy's CLI registers nothing, and the Electron app's nessy:// scheme is registered by the installed bundle itself (electron-builder.yml:82-84 -> CFBundleURLTypes / NSIS registry / .desktop MimeType), so no runtime settings key could 'prevent registration entirely'. The scheme is also load-bearing here in a way claude-cli:// is not: it carries the OAuth callback (nessy://auth-callback, packages/shared/src/auth/callback-server.ts:41) and the app's own internal navigation routing (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/system.ts:283-312). If the sibling auto-send concern is real, the only achievable control in this fork sits at the HANDLING boundary -- handleDeepLink (apps/electron/src/main/deep-link.ts:235) or the `send` action param -- and must keep auth-callback working. That is a different finding at a different layer, not this Claude settings key.
